extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency information managers, STI program managers, agency policy and IRM officials implementing OMB Circular A-130
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and an implementation/template checklist for Federal agencies to manage Scientific and Technical Information (STI) consistent with OMB Circular A-130, covering planning, collection, dissemination, records management, safeguards, interagency sharing, and IT/IRM issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify guidance concerning public access to agency information
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB’s intent in the Circular regarding the extent to which agencies are to provide access to STI to all citizens should be clarified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientists and other technical individuals form the primary audience for the STI. Currently, agencies focus on particular customer segments proactively and address the needs of the general public by making information available on demand. The Circular does not clearly define whether “announcement” of the existence of information is sufficient for compliance or whether agencies must actively promote and deliver full text of the information. The public’s right to the information should be preserved; however, the extent to which agencies should or must reach out to the general public should be clarified so that agencies can allocate scarce resources most effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balancing A-130 and other national and international STI requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must align A-130 policies (e.g., avoid exclusive/restrictive distribution arrangements; timeliness and equity of dissemination) with realities of international exchange, cooperative partnerships, technology transfer, and other statutory/ program objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: STI is international in scope and increasingly viewed as a commodity with military/economic value. The prohibition on Federal agencies restricting reuse of information can weaken the ability to deal with international partners who may require redistribution restrictions as a condition of exchange. Agencies may legitimately accept restrictions when the value of information to the U.S. is sufficiently great. The Circular is silent on handling international information received on exchange (except treaty-level agreements). Agencies need guidance or provisions to allow selective exemption of international STI from the A-130 reuse provision when unrestricted reuse would cut off access, and to resolve apparent conflicts between A-130 and other goals such as technology transfer and international cooperation. Example: NASA’s exchange agreements and difficulties protecting partner data under FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolve conflicts between A-130 objectives and other Government initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide mechanisms to ensure A-130 interpretation does not undermine other important goals (e.g., technology transfer, international cooperation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It may be in the interest of the U.S. Government to exempt certain international STI from the A-130 reuse provision or to clarify sections to allow selective withholding when domestic/international agreements call for it. Alternatively, provide additional guidance to agencies on resolving conflicts between A-130 and other Federal programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for uniform approaches to information access and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Government STI lacks a standard 'look and feel', has duplicative systems, and lacks standards for data quality, making navigation and finding information difficult in the electronic environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Government needs a cohesive electronic image and a 'selected mode of operation' for information services. Voluntary and Federal information processing standards should be followed whenever possible, but planning and implementation guidance is needed given rapid technology change. Standardization of identifiers (URLs, URNs, report numbers, ISSNs analogs) and electronic document identifiers is fundamental to making government information findable and available. Agencies should develop uniform approaches to home pages, access to resources, and a uniform package for organization, presentation, and retrieval of government information resources, using the STI community as a developmental focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor selected mode of operation for Government information services
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB should initiate and support an effort to develop a selected mode of operation (uniform approaches) for agency information services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A task force representing STI communities should develop guidance on organization, presentation, and retrieval that is scalable (STI covers a broad range of data types; STI users are a manageable subset of the general public).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency information sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote and institutionalize interagency cooperative efforts for sharing STI to satisfy information needs and reduce duplication, while recognizing legal limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Circular urges agencies to look to interagency or intergovernmental sharing to satisfy new information needs. Sharing of information systems (not content) is a policy requirement 'to the extent practicable and legally permissible.' Current sharing is often ad hoc and discipline-specific; multidisciplinary R&D and environmental monitoring require broader interagency cooperation. Recommendation: provide for STI sharing under appropriate sections of A-130 and officially encourage/institutionalize cooperative efforts such as CENDI, modeled on bodies like the Federal Geographic Data Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Management Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: STI planning should be life-cycle planning and integrated with agency planning and budgeting processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should consider the form of the information, its content, customers, use, and levels of required protection. Managed STI should have practical utility. Specific agency questions: Does the agency have an integrated life-cycle information management planning system for STI? Are STI life-cycle phases viewed in relationship and impact on one another? Is impact on dissemination processes/goals articulated? What mechanisms determine effects on the public and ensure consultation? How is interagency/intragovernmental/commercial cooperation handled to avoid duplication? Is STI planning linked to IT and systems development? What training ensures employees have appropriate skills? How is level/method of protection determined and risk measured? Is there a policy regarding use of voluntary/FIPS standards? How are privacy rights handled? What documentation ensures management accountability? Are records management and archival responsibilities integrated into systems development? How is public access provided?

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Collection
rubrics_metrics.description: STI collection and creation activities should support the agency’s functions and minimize burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can STI collection/creation be justified as part of proper performance of agency functions? Does the managed STI have practical utility?

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Information Collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic STI collection techniques should be evaluated against criteria including volume, audience, frequency, structural stability, and conversion considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review collection techniques with respect to: large volume of data collected; information reaches large proportion of public; collection occurs frequently; structure/format/definition stability over time; routine conversion to electronic format; public access/readiness to maintain data electronically; whether mandatory electronic reporting would impose substantial costs or adverse impacts (especially on State/local governments and small businesses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency records management programs should properly account for STI and comply with NARA requirements; responsible employees should be trained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Are STI records available regardless of form/medium? Are STI retention schedules approved by NARA? Is there adequate training of employees/contractors regarding STI records management responsibilities? Are records management and archival responsibilities integrated into STI systems development?

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing Information to the Public
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should help the public locate government information; information provided should be consistent with agency missions and balance usefulness against cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions for agencies: What are requirements to disseminate STI within your mission and are they being met? Are STI organization, activities, programs, systems of records, etc., provided to the public for access? How are FOIA and Privacy Act implemented regarding STI? Considerations for dissemination planning include balancing maximizing usefulness vs minimizing cost; assurance of equity and timeliness; utilizing all dissemination channels (Federal, State/local governments, libraries, private sector); aids to help the public locate STI maintained by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Dissemination Management System
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should have a management system for all STI dissemination products that addresses user needs, depositories, sources of STI, and compliance with A-130.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissemination should be timely and use all channels. Maintain an inventory of all agency STI dissemination products. Provide catalogs/directories to help locate products. Identify when STI products come from another agency. Ensure access for persons with disabilities. Make STI publications available to depository libraries and provide specified electronic products to GPO as appropriate. Communicate with public and State/local governments to ensure products meet needs. Provide notice procedures when initiating/modifying/terminating significant STI products. Have plans/procedures to ensure policies/practices comply with the Circular. Agency questions: Do you have a dissemination management system? How does it assure necessity of products for agency functions? How determine if another source can fulfill dissemination responsibilities? Do you maintain an inventory? Which electronic products are provided to GPO? How communicate with public and state/local governments?

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding Improperly Restrictive Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution practices should be reviewed regarding timeliness and equity of use and reuse, resale, or redissemination; user charges should be set at the cost of STI dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review for exclusive, restricted, or other distribution arrangements that prevent timely and equitable availability. Identify any restrictions on reuse/resale/redissemination and any fees/royalties. Ensure user charges equal dissemination cost and document how costs are calculated. Identify statutory requirements that differ from policy. Determine if special STI efforts benefit specific identifiable groups and how they're charged. Are any charges less than dissemination cost and is there justification? Are there any exceptions approved by OMB?

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Information Dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Use electronic media/formats and public networks as appropriate to increase accessibility and usefulness while avoiding imposing substantial acquisition or training costs on users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure electronic dissemination uses appropriate media/formats and public networks. Electronic dissemination should not impose substantial acquisition or training costs on users, especially State/local governments and small businesses. Agency questions: To what extent does the agency use electronic media and formats? Is STI developed/maintained electronically? Are large, highly detailed volumes provided and is electronic media the format of choice? Are STI products disseminated frequently? Does electronic dissemination impose substantial acquisition/training costs on users?

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should determine and fully implement appropriate protection for STI and ensure compliance with applicable limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How does the agency determine proper level of protection to minimize risk from loss, misuse, unauthorized access or modification? How does the agency limit collection of STI that identifies individuals to that necessary for agency functions? How does the agency limit sharing of proprietary or personal STI to what is legally authorized and ensure confidentiality? Does the agency have Privacy Act STI, and how is that information provided to individuals consistent with the Privacy Act?

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and Performance Measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use work process redesign and information technology to improve effectiveness/efficiency; perform life-cycle benefit-cost analyses for information systems supporting STI per OMB guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Life-cycle benefit-cost analyses should be established for each information system supporting STI in accordance with OMB guidelines. Analyses should consider effectiveness of program delivery, efficiency of administration, reduction in burden on the public, and be proportional to investment size. Are benefit-cost analyses consistent with OMB A-94? Are they undertaken agency-wide for major systems and part of ongoing management oversight? Is there a process of post-implementation reviews to validate benefits and document effective practices and lessons learned?

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Information Resources Management (IRM) Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: IRM planning, incorporating STI, should promote fulfillment of the agency’s mission and address statutory requirements (e.g., 5 CFR 1320, 44 USC 3506).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning should address information collection burden and preparation of a five-year plan. Ensure existing/planned major information systems for STI are reflected. Include planned IT acquisitions for STI, relate major systems and acquisitions to support STI mission, include computer security considerations, coordinate IRM planning with strategic, human resources, and financial planning. Agency questions: Does your agency have a strategic IRM planning process that includes STI? Does coverage of STI reflect/anticipate changes in mission, policy, technology, or resources? Are STI requirements included in the five-year plan?

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Systems Management Oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Management and technology frameworks should document linkages between missions, needs, information content, and IT capabilities; ensure systems meet mission requirements and are reviewed periodically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each information system supporting STI meets agency mission requirements with periodic reviews to determine if mission requirements have changed, what maintenance is needed, and whether the system continues to fulfill anticipated mission requirements. Ensure accountability for system management throughout life cycle. Provide training for users of Federal information resources supporting STI. Protect prerogatives of State, local, and tribal governments vis-à-vis systems. Coordinate decisionmaking about information, human, financial, and other resources so systems proceed in a timely fashion to life cycle milestones. Is the financial management system supporting STI in conformance with OMB Circular A-127? Is there an agency-wide management or IRM committee with STI representation?

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Information Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that STI systems support the agency’s requirements and document linkages between mission needs, information content, and technology capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the agency’s management and technical framework for using information resources, documenting linkages between STI mission needs, information content, and IT capabilities. Ensure systems support agency requirements and that decisionmaking about resources is coordinated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of Information Technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice full and open competition in IT acquisition; incorporate off-the-shelf software when cost-effective; conform to OMB Circular A-109; consider individuals with disabilities in acquisition procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisition procedures should ensure full and open competition and consider use of off-the-shelf solutions when cost-effective. Conformance with OMB Circular A-109 should be ensured. Acquisition procedures should consider accessibility and needs of individuals with disabilities.
